chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Jundab, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And We have indeed made the Word reach them, so that they may take heed.
He عليه السلام said: “An Imam to an Imam.”

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam addressed in the narration
key_terms.إِمَامٌ: an Imam; a divinely guided leader in context
key_terms.قَوْلِ اللَّهِ: the word or saying of Allah, referring here to the Qur'anic verse
key_terms.وَصَّلْنَا: We caused to reach continuously or conveyed in succession
key_terms.يَتَذَكَّرُونَ: they may remember, take heed, or be mindful

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith interpret the verse “And We have indeed made the Word reach them” in relation to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a Qur'anic commentary in which the verse is understood through the continuity of divine guidance passing from one Imam to another. Its significance lies in linking the Qur'anic phrase to the doctrine of the Imamate and the ongoing transmission of authoritative guidance.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Jundab who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Allah<sup>asws</sup> Mighty and Majestic
28:51] And We have Made the Word to reach them so that they may be mindful.
en.sarwar: 18. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abdallah ibn Jundab who has said the following.
“I asked abu al-Hassan (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious.
“We sent Our guidance to them so that perhaps they might take heed.” [28:51]
The Imam (a.s.) said, “It means the one Imam after the other.”
